page.layout: One column of running text, with fraction worked examples set in display between the paragraphs. Above the text, a line of mixed numbers. Printed page number and running head at the top. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Hic priorem notam per inferiorem multiplico, & superiore addo, dicens: semel 4 sunt 4, addito 1, sunt 5, quæ infra scribo, & Denominatorem subnoto. Deinde dico bis 8 sunt 16, additis 3, sunt 19, quę infra scribo & Denominatore subnoto, hoc modo:
Hæcres usui est in sequentibus, ut faci-lior fiat operatio.

Cùm Fractio majoribus numeris scripta est, minimo quàm potest fieri numero exprimatur, inquire igitur numerum quemcunque, qui ambos, superiorem scilicet & inferiorem ita exacte dividat, ut nihil superfit, quotientes ad latus scribito.
Hic Numerator dividitur ꝑ 2, & 2 in 14 continentur 7: Denominator dividitur per 2, & 2 in 24 continentur 12. Iam Fractio minimo quàm potest fieri numero exprimitur, sic:
Hujusmodi verò Fractionem 15 / 105 ad minimam sic redigo, dicens: 3 in 15 conti-nentur

page.notes: The fractions are set in display as stacked numerators and denominators. They are rendered here as lines, with the fraction bars shown by spacing and slashes. The printed "p 2" in the Numerator sentence is read as ꝑ (per) with some doubt. The word "fnquire" in the printed text is read as "inquire". The line "Hæcres" is printed with no space after the initial word, as the printer set it. Page is otherwise clean; no catchword or signature is visible.
